gaps.sentence: I looked everywhere, but I couldn't find my keys ___.
gaps.explanation: After a negative verb, 'anywhere' is used; 'somewhere' belongs to affirmative sentences.

gaps.sentence: It cost a great ___ of money to repair the roof.
gaps.explanation: 'A great deal of' is used with uncountable nouns like money; 'a great lot of' and 'a great plenty of' do not exist.

gaps.hint: general statement without 'the' — 'people' has no article
gaps.explanation: 'Most people' means people in general; 'most of' needs 'the' (most of the people).

gaps.sentence: ___ the rooms in the hotel have a sea view; the rest face the car park.
gaps.explanation: Before 'the rooms' a partitive is needed: Some of; 'all/none' contradict the context.

gaps.sentence: He took ___ notice of the warning and carried on as before.
gaps.explanation: 'Take little notice of' means to pay hardly any attention; 'notice' is uncountable here.

gaps.sentence: We had very ___ rain this spring, so the garden suffered.
gaps.explanation: 'Little' means not much and is used with uncountables; the garden suffering shows an insufficient amount.

gaps.sentence: We haven't received ___ information about the delay.
gaps.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable, so 'much' is required in the negative sentence.

gaps.sentence: ___ of my friends knew about the concert, so I went on my own.
gaps.explanation: 'None of my friends' means zero friends; 'no' cannot stand before 'of' and 'nothing' is not a quantifier here.
